nodes.summary: Writing $M(n)$ for the number of noncrossing perfect matchings of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, The point $0$ is matched to some $j + 1$ with $0 \le j < n$, and splitting off the arc $\{0, j + 1\}$ leaves independent noncrossing matchings of the $j$ points inside it and of the $n - 1 - j$ points to its right.
nodes.title: Catalan recursion for noncrossing matchings

nodes.summary: The number of noncrossing perfect matchings of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $C_{n/2}$ when $n$ is even and $0$ when $n$ is odd; in particular there is exactly one (empty) matching of the empty set.
nodes.title: Counting noncrossing perfect matchings

nodes.summary: For every $k$, there is no noncrossing pair partition of $\{1, \dots, 2k + 1\}$. This is the combinatorial reason why the odd moments of the semicircle law vanish and why only even powers contribute in the moment method.
nodes.title: There is no pair partition of an odd number of points

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 0$, the number of noncrossing partitions of $\{1, \dots, 2k\}$ all of whose blocks have two elements is Mathlib's `catalan k`. For instance there are $C_2 = 2$ noncrossing pairings of four points, $\{\{1,2\},\{3,4\}\}$ and $\{\{1,4\},\{2,3\}\}$, while $\{\{1,3\},\{2,4\}\}$ crosses.
nodes.title: Noncrossing pair partitions of `{1, …, 2k}` are counted by the Catalan number `C_k`

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the number of noncrossing pair partitions of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ is $C_{n/2}$ if $n$ is even and $0$ if $n$ is odd. This is the form used for the moments of the semicircle law, which are $\int x^n \, d\sigma(x) = \#\{\pi \in NC(n) : \pi \text{ a pair partition}\}$ for all $n$.
nodes.title: Counting noncrossing pair partitions

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a *noncrossing perfect matching* of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ if it maps $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to itself, has no fixed point there, is an involution there ($f(f(i)) = i$), is the identity from $n$ on, and its arcs $\{a, f(a)\}$ are nested or disjoint: whenever $a < b < f(a)$, also $a < f(b) < f(a)$.
nodes.title: Noncrossing perfect matching

nodes.summary: A set partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (a `Finpartition` of `Fin n`) is a *pair partition* if every block of $P$ has exactly two elements. A pair partition exists only when $n$ is even, and for $n = 2k$ the pair partitions are the perfect matchings of $2k$ points; the noncrossing ones are counted by the Catalan number $C_k$.
nodes.title: Pair partition

nodes.summary: For a noncrossing perfect matching $f$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the partition of `Fin n` whose blocks are the arcs $\{i, f(i)\}$. It is built as the partition into classes of the equivalence relation "$y = x$ or $y = f(x)$", which is an equivalence relation because $f$ is an involution. It is a noncrossing pair partition.
nodes.title: The pair partition of a matching

nodes.summary: `NCMatching n` is the subtype of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ that are noncrossing perfect matchings of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. It is finite, since a matching is determined by its restriction to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and its cardinality is counted by Counting noncrossing perfect matchings.
nodes.title: The type of noncrossing perfect matchings

nodes.summary: The partner map is a bijection from the noncrossing pair partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to the noncrossing perfect matchings of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, with inverse the pair partition of a matching.
nodes.title: Noncrossing pair partitions are noncrossing perfect matchings

nodes.summary: For a set partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $i < n$, the partner of $i$ is $\bigl(\sum_{x \in B(i)} x\bigr) - i$, where $B(i)$ is the block of $i$; for $i \ge n$ it is $i$. When $P$ is a pair partition, $B(i) = \{i, j\}$ with $j \ne i$, so the partner of $i$ is $j$. The sum formula makes the map total without choosing an element.
nodes.title: Partner map of a pair partition

nodes.summary: Let $n = j + m + 2$. The noncrossing perfect matchings $f$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $f(0) = j + 1$ are in bijection with pairs $(g, h)$ of noncrossing perfect matchings of $\{0, \dots, j-1\}$ and of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$:
